edges.description: Presynaptic blockade of motor nerve signal transmission causes descending flaccid neuromuscular paralysis.
Presynaptic neuromuscular blockade of bulbar and respiratory musculature leads to ventilatory failure.
Postsynaptic blockade at the neuromuscular junction produces flaccid paralysis.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular blockade of respiratory muscles impairs ventilation and causes respiratory failure.
Depletion of fibrinogen and clotting factors in venom-induced consumption coagulopathy results in incoagulable blood and spontaneous systemic hemorrhage.
Severe systemic hemorrhage and intravascular volume depletion contribute to circulatory shock and hypotension.
Microvascular coagulopathy and hemorrhagic shock contribute to downstream renal injury.
Extracellular matrix digestion and local tissue injury produce rapid swelling at the bite site.

Renal tubular and microvascular injury from systemic envenoming results in clinical acute kidney injury.

nodes.description: Presynaptic phospholipase A2 beta-neurotoxins (such as Mojave toxin) trigger intracellular Ca2+ and arachidonic acid cascades, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and neurotransmitter overload in excitatory synapses, leading to presynaptic blockade of nerve signals that is relatively refractory to antivenom and anticholinesterase reversal once established.

evidence.reference_title: Neurocellular Stress Response to Mojave Type A Rattlesnake Venom: Study of Molecular Mechanisms Using Human iPSC-Derived Neural Stem Cell Model.
evidence.snippet: The MTX, which is composed of heterodimers of basic and acidic phospholipase-A2, co-opts the host arachidonic acid and Ca2+ second messenger mechanisms and triggers multiple signaling cascades, such as the activation of MAPKs and NF-κB-regulated proinflammatory genes; the neurotransmitter overload in excitatory synapses leading to a presynaptic blockade of nerve signals; and the upregulation of unfolded protein response (UPR) due to the depletion of Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum.
